where: Section 2, definition line after the dP/dz formula
problem: The text defines dM/dz = S as the shear force in N, but then writes qb = −(1/h)(dM/dz) = S/h. With that definition qb would be −S/h, not +S/h. The worked example uses dM/dz = −20 000 N with S = +20 000 N, so the stated definition contradicts both the formula and step 9. A student following the definition gets the opposite sign for the bending flow.
fix: Define dM/dz = −S, where S is the magnitude of the shear force in N (positive when the moment falls outward). Then qb = −(1/h)(dM/dz) = S/h is consistent with the worked example.

problem: 'Both leanings put the boom axis at a small angle to the span and both feed the same term' and 'A swept boom's transverse component acts both through the depth and chordwise' are wrong for sweep alone. The boom force Pi = M yi Ai/Ixx depends only on the vertical distance yi from the neutral axis. A boom that leans only in plan (sweep) has the same yi and the same dPi/dz, so sweep does not feed the q = −ΣdPi/dz term at all. Its chordwise component P dx/dz is balanced by a chordwise circulation of shear flow (a constant q0 round the box), not by the vertical web flow.
fix: Say that sweep gives the boom force a chordwise component P dx/dz, which produces a chordwise circulation of shear flow and a torque about the span axis, but does not add a term to q = −ΣdPi/dz because Pi depends only on yi. The vertical taper term comes only from the change of depth with z.

problem: 'The taper flow is largest near the root, where M is largest and the depth changes fastest per unit length' is misleading. For a linear taper dh/dz is constant along the span, so the depth does not change fastest at the root. Also qtaper = M h'/h² has h² in the denominator, so qtaper is not guaranteed to be largest at the root for a strong taper.
fix: Say: for a linear taper dh/dz is the same at every station; qtaper = M h'/h² is usually largest inboard because M is largest there, but the h² denominator also matters.

problem: The caption says 'The bending moment gradient sets the boom force', but the boom force is set by the bending moment M itself (P = M/h). The gradient dM/dz sets dP/dz and the ordinary bending flow, not the boom force.
fix: Write: 'The bending moment sets the boom force; its gradient sets dP/dz and the bending flow. The boom slope turns part of the boom force into a transverse component that appears as a taper shear flow.'

problem: The text says 'dP/dz picks up a second term'. In general, differentiating Pi = M yi Ai/Ixx gives two extra terms, one from dyi/dz and one from dIxx/dz. Only in the two-boom spar do these combine into a single geometry term.
fix: Say 'dP/dz picks up extra terms from dyi/dz and dIxx/dz (in the two-boom spar these combine into one geometry term)'.
